solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lone Conservative oddly in some error

parts.note: lone means sole, single

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the words in some

explanation.surface: A lone Tory voter strangely caught up in some mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the odd letters of 'in some', giving ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A solecism is a blunder, especially a grammatical mistake or breach of etiquette.

clue.text: Boxers giving jabs round centre of midriff

indicators.note: round means the jabs surround the central letter

parts.note: jabs are shots, as in injections

indicators.note: centre of picks the middle letter of the word midriff

explanation.surface: Boxers throwing punches around the middle of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters, but it is the underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are a loose kind of men's underpants, hence shorts.

clue.text: Room in place containing miniature that's mounted

indicators.note: containing says the word for place holds the other inside it

parts.note: to lay is to put or place

indicators.note: mounted in a down clue means the word climbs, read upwards

parts.note: wee means tiny, miniature

explanation.surface: Space in a display holding a little painting hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's mounted' reverses WEE to EEW, as in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is room to manoeuvre, scope or latitude.

clue.text: Starts to crack open someone's head employing sap

definitions.text: Starts to crack open someone's head employing sap

indicators.note: starts to asks for the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Breaking a person's skull open with a blackjack.
explanation.walkthrough: The initials of the six words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a club or blackjack, also called a sap; to cosh someone is to strike their head with one.

clue.text: The woman's skill taking little time for love

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the pair holds the small words

parts.note: the woman is SHE, with the 's read as is
wee is Scottish for little
art is skill

explanation.surface: Her talent for love, given a little time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' signals a container; the apostrophe in 'The woman's' is read as 'is', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is a term of endearment, like darling or sweetheart.

clue.text: Imprudent individual caught by this compiler's work

indicators.note: by means placed beside, so these letters come next to the setter's work

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves, so this compiler's is MY
OP is short for opus, a work
I as in the single individual, the first person
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A reckless person gets trapped by the setter's own puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sighted in the figurative sense: lacking foresight, hence unwise.

clue.text: The old left, more depressed and more cowardly

parts.note: ye is an old form of the
lower means more downcast, more depressed

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned person left, sadder and more spineless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' gives YE, archaic for the.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow means cowardly, so the comparative means more cowardly.

clue.text: States with power careless consuming energy

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: consuming means eating up, so the careless word takes energy inside

parts.note: remiss means negligent, careless
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Countries with power, careless and burning up energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like countries but is a verb: asserts as a premise.
explanation.definitionFit: To premise is to set down as a basis for argument, so premises means asserts or states.

clue.text: One records group covering another group

indicators.note: covering means the first group wraps round the second

parts.note: a caste is a social group or class
a set is a group

explanation.surface: One band covers another band's songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'records' is a verb here, not a noun for discs; 'covering' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a tape cartridge that records audio, so it is one thing that records.

clue.text: Lover's tepid about pass

indicators.note: the clue words Lover's tepid are about the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A lukewarm lover makes a half-hearted pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pass' seems to be a romantic advance, but it is the verb meaning go beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstep a limit is to go past or exceed it.

clue.text: Prepare force to overturn armadas

indicators.note: overturn says the joined words are turned over and read backwards

parts.note: to steel oneself is to prepare for something hard
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: Getting ready to force the enemy's naval fleets to capsize.
explanation.definitionFit: Armadas and fleets are both large groups of warships.

clue.text: Go to purchase an undergarment producing mockery

indicators.note: purchase means grip or hold, so the attempt grips the garment inside it

parts.note: a go is an attempt or try
an gives the article A
a vest is a sleeveless undergarment

explanation.surface: Trying to buy a vest turns into a farce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purchase' looks like shopping but means a grip, so TRY grips A VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is an absurd or grotesque imitation, a sham or mockery of something.

clue.text: Acolyte retrospectively concerned with sin

indicators.note: looking back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: on in the sense of about or concerning
vice is wickedness, sin

explanation.surface: An altar server looks back on some past wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a newcomer or beginner, an acolyte also being a junior church assistant.

clue.text: Squalor of poor in line seems hollow

indicators.note: in places the word for poor inside the word for line

parts.note: a file is a line, as in single file
thin means poor, meagre

indicators.note: hollow means emptied of its middle, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: The squalor of the poor queuing seems empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' looks like an anagram signal but gives THIN, which goes 'in' FILE; 'hollow' leaves SS of seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthiness and squalor both mean dirt and wretchedness.

clue.text: Withdrawal of English credit rejected in split

indicators.note: in says these letters go inside the word for split

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split

indicators.note: rejected says the word for credit is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: merit is credit or praise deserved

explanation.surface: An English loan turned down amid a rift leads to someone stepping back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses MERIT to TIREM; E and TIREM go 'in' RENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Retirement is withdrawal from work or from active life.

clue.text: Stud perhaps more hasty hiding butt, almost

indicators.note: hiding means holding out of sight, so the shortened end goes within

parts.note: faster means quicker, more hasty

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a butt is an end, as of a cigarette

explanation.surface: A stallion quicker to conceal its rear, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts END to EN, which FASTER is 'hiding'. 'Stud perhaps' defines by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud, such as a press stud, is one kind of fastener.

clue.text: General charged without resistance taking charge initially

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the shortened word holds the letter
without means lacking, so that letter is removed

parts.note: electric means charged, as of an atmosphere
R is the physics symbol for resistance

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word charge

explanation.surface: A charged military commander, without resistance, takes charge first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops R from ELECTRIC to give ELECTIC, which is 'taking' C.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclectic means broad and wide-ranging, drawing on many sources, so general.

clue.text: This answer isn't stupid!

parts.note: the answer means stupid, yet read as two parts it says lacking a hint, which this entry, having a hint, does not

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer to read 'without a clue': true of no entry here, since every entry has one, so 'this answer isn't' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Clueless means stupid or ignorant, having no idea.

clue.text: Speed after group mostly in top speed

indicators.note: after says the first word comes after the rest
in places the shortened group inside the word for top

parts.note: ace means excellent, top-notch

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a cell is a small group, as in a political cell
rate means speed, pace

explanation.surface: A cycling team chasing top speed.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'speed' twice: the first is wordplay, the last the definition. 'mostly', 'in' and 'after' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: To accelerate is to speed up, to go faster.

clue.text: Stages raised in part, so raised

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Platforms put up partly, so lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: Added the indicator 'in' to the draft's hidden step, which it signals. 'raised' in a down clue sends ARTSOR upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostra are raised platforms for speakers, a kind of stage.

clue.text: Sat on the throne, we hear, and showered

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a monarch who sat on the throne reigned

explanation.surface: The king sat in state, and then had a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sat on the throne' tempts a toilet joke; it means ruled.
explanation.definitionFit: Rained and showered both describe precipitation, or things falling down in quantity.

clue.text: Reportedly one could supply bargain basement

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a seller is one who could supply a bargain

explanation.surface: A shop in the basement is said to supply cheap deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bargain basement' reads as one phrase, but bargain belongs with the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground room beneath a building, a basement.

clue.text: Ancient Egyptian city, virtually second to none

indicators.note: virtually means almost all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: second to none means the best

explanation.surface: An old city of Egypt ranked almost the finest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' cuts the final T from THE BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Thebes was a capital of ancient Egypt on the Nile, near modern Luxor.

clue.text: Navigation chart describing island span

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing a line round, so the chart encloses the island

parts.note: to plot is to chart a course
an age is a span of time

explanation.surface: A sea chart showing an island across a certain distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means tracing round, so PLOT goes round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilotage is the skill or act of steering a vessel, especially through coastal waters.

clue.text: The woman's chasing ultimate bottom!

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the woman's word comes second

parts.note: net means final, as in a net result
her is the possessive for the woman

explanation.surface: A woman in hot pursuit of the finest backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' is used as an adjective, as in nether regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Nether means lower or lowest, as in the underworld's nether regions.

clue.text: Lookout dispatched message first to last

parts.note: dispatched means sent off

indicators.note: first to last says the opening letter of the word for message moves to its end

parts.note: a line is a short message, as in drop me a line

explanation.surface: A watchman sent a note, from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to last' turns LINE into INEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a guard or sentry keeping watch.

clue.text: Stop assuming chimera's exterior's given new form

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the word for stop takes in the outer letters

parts.note: a rest is a stop or pause

indicators.note: the exterior of a word is its outside letters, first and last

explanation.surface: Halting a monster's outer shell remade into a new shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exterior's' gives CA, the outer letters of chimera, which REST is 'assuming'.
explanation.definitionFit: To recast is to remould or reshape, so recast means remodelled.

clue.text: Run down by one man in Ibiza?

indicators.note: by means alongside, so one sits next to the word for run down

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to run someone down is to criticise or slander them

explanation.surface: A man knocked down by a holidaymaker on the Spanish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a man in Ibiza lives on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An islander is an inhabitant of an island, which Ibiza is.
